section.name: Embedded databases
section.p: mvn -B -ntp test runs the database-backed regression tests against both H2 and HSQLDB, as well as the existing JDBC test doubles. HSQLDB uses the jdk8 classifier of version 2.7.4; its ordinary artifact requires Java 11. Each database fixture gets a unique embedded database, which shuts down when its last physical connection closes.

section.name: Docker databases
section.p: With a running Docker daemon, use mvn -B -ntp -Pdocker-it verify to also run the shared connection-pool tests against PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle Database Express Edition (XE), and Microsoft SQL Server. The Docker Maven plugin starts the databases, waits for the final server startup log after initialization, and passes dynamically allocated ports to Failsafe. Maven removes the containers and their volumes after the tests, including after test failures.

The Maven commands are the same on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Docker must run Linux containers; the images initialize their databases, and the tests configure additional database and XA permissions through JDBC. No host shell scripts or bind-mounted initialization files are required. The JDBC drivers support Java 8.

Oracle XE and SQL Server use linux/amd64 images and require a compatible x86-64 Docker runtime. On ARM hosts, including Apple Silicon, use an x86-64 Docker host or virtual machine. Specifying the image platform alone does not guarantee that emulation will work. See the Oracle XE image guidance and SQL Server platform requirements. SQL Server runs the Developer edition for testing.

To reduce memory usage or select databases supported by your Docker runtime, pass a comma-separated list of aliases: postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle, and sqlserver. The same selection controls container startup and test execution. Quote the complete property argument in PowerShell as shown here:

Use verify, since stopping at integration-test omits container cleanup and test-result verification. A missing daemon or failed database startup fails the build rather than skipping tests. -DskipITs skips both container startup and integration tests. With the configured Failsafe 3.6.1, -DskipTests skips only Surefire tests; it still compiles the test sources and runs the Docker integration tests. -Dmaven.test.skip=true also skips test compilation and Failsafe, so it must not be used for an integration-only run.
To run only the Docker integration tests, use the following command. Coverage collection and checks are disabled for this partial suite; the main CI build enforces the full-suite coverage thresholds.

The shared tests cover pool reuse, validation, invalidation, state restoration, rollback on return, CPDS logical handles, prepared statements, generated keys, and managed local/XA transactions with Geronimo and Narayana. XA commit tests enlist a second resource to exercise two-phase commit. PostgreSQL enables max_prepared_transactions for these tests. Oracle grants the test user access to the XA recovery views and package. SQL Server installs the JDBC XA procedures and grants the test login membership in SqlJDBCXAUser before running the tests.

Image versions are pinned in dbcp.docker.postgresql.image, dbcp.docker.mysql.image, dbcp.docker.mariadb.image, dbcp.docker.oracle.image, and dbcp.docker.sqlserver.image and can be overridden with Maven properties. Oracle startup has a separate timeout, dbcp.docker.oracle.waitMillis; the other databases use dbcp.docker.waitMillis. Ports bind to loopback by default. For a remote Docker host, set DOCKER_HOST and override dbcp.docker.bindAddress with a suitable address on that host. The configured database users and passwords are only for these disposable test databases.

section.name: Reports and cleanup
section.p: Surefire reports are in target/surefire-reports; Failsafe reports are in target/failsafe-reports. The database is included in parameterized test display names, and container logs appear in Maven output. Docker CI jobs run each database separately on Java 8 and 25 using Linux x86-64 runners. These jobs skip Surefire tests and JaCoCo. The normal Java matrix runs the unit tests, both embedded databases, quality checks, and coverage checks without Docker.

Both matrices run concurrently. The required Java CI results check succeeds only when both matrices succeed, including their cleanup steps. The experimental Java build remains allowed to fail. The required check is configured in the repository's ASF ruleset.

Remove only the listed test containers with docker rm -f -v <container-id>. CI performs this cleanup automatically, including after startup failures.
